{{Quote|Stop that ship! Blast 'em!|An unnamed stormtrooper in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Docking Bay 94/Legends|Docking Bay 94]]|<ref name="SWEIV:ANH" />}}
The '''RT-97C heavy blaster rifle''' was a designation given to certain model of offensive blaster weaponry that produced more devastating results than its lesser cousin, the [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]].

==Description==
The RT-97C [[Heavy blaster rifle/Legends|heavy blaster rifle]] featured an extra long galvenning [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]] for a finer alignment of the energy beam projectile that increased firing range.

It contained three separate [[Scope/Legends|scopes]] to increase accuracy and versatility. Its first scope was a [[Thermal imaging scanner/Legends|thermal scanner]] that was capable of detecting and enhancing life forms that generated heat. Its second scope was a [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper]] scope that automatically calculated range and adjusted the rifle's collimating components. Its third scope was a passive [[infrared scope]] that used heat imaging technology. It also rendered elements like rain, smoke, dust, and darkness transparent and it could transmit visual data to stormtrooper's optical sensors.

Although cumbersome compared with the [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech]] [[E-11]], it was the preferred weapon of Imperial [[Desert stormtrooper/Legends|sandtroopers]]<ref name="Star Wars Blueprints: The Ultimate Collection" /> and the [[Stormtrooper sniper/Legends|Stormsnipers]].<ref name="Assault Team">''[[Star Wars: Assault Team]]''</ref>

{{Weapon-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The early [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]]-era German [[Wikipedia:MG-15|MG-15]] machine gun provided the basis for this 'in universe' weapon. The MG-15, with its distinct saddle drum magazines, was used by [[Wikipedia:Luftwaffe|Luftwaffe]] air crews for air defense during WWII as well as the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luftwaffe_Field_Divisions Luftwaffe field Divisions] who used the weapon in a light machine gun role due to shortages of more adequate weapons like the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MG_34 MG-34]. The scope on the blaster is a WWII-vintage British No32 telescopic sight designed for use with the Bren light machine gun and the Lee-Enfield No.4T sniper rifle.

Until 2008 this heavy blaster had not received an official [[canon]] designation in any Star Wars reference material, and was simply referred to by fans as the 'MG-15'. It was finally termed the "BlasTech RT-97C" in the ''[[Star Wars Blueprints: The Ultimate Collection]]'' ([[Dorling Kindersley|DK Books]], 2008). The name references the artists of the blueprints [[Chris Reiff]] and [[Chris Trevas]], and the year they first met - '''R'''(eiff)'''T'''(revas)-(19)'''97C'''(hris).
